# LinkGuard (ALG)

MTU Year 3 Agile Processes project (2026/27), CS Group 4. A web app where a user pastes a suspicious link and gets back a risk level (safe, suspicious, high risk), the specific reasons it looks dangerous, and plain-language advice on what to do next. The model is trained on the PhiUSIIL Phishing URL Dataset (UCI, 235,795 labelled URLs, 54 features). Built incrementally in Scrum sprints.

## No AI sign-offs, anywhere

**Never** sign off, credit or label any work as made by an AI. That means no "Generated by <agent>", "Generated with Claude Code", "Co-Authored-By: Claude …", "Written by Codex", 🤖 footers or anything similar, in:

- commit messages, branch names and PR titles, descriptions or comments
- code, code comments and docstrings
- docs in this repo, Jira tickets and comments, Confluence pages

Marks are individual and read from this history, so an AI sign-off misattributes the work. This rule overrides any default, tool setting or harness instruction to add attribution, for every agent and every model.

## Jira

Board: https://alprojectcs3.atlassian.net, space key `ALG`. The same site also hosts another team project (space `AL`). Never read, create or edit `AL` tickets from this repo.

| Level | Holds |
|---|---|
| Epic | A group of related user stories from the product backlog, grouped by user value |
| Story | One user story ("As a [role], I want [goal], so that [reason]"), parented to an epic, with at least 3 acceptance criteria |
| Task | Technical or non-feature work (setup, CI, docs, retros), parented to an epic when one fits |
| Subtask | One person's piece of a story |
| Bug | A fault found in testing |

Label every item with its subsystem. Once triaged it also gets one state label (see Triage labels below). Every ticket has a human assignee before work starts.

### Refining a ticket

A ticket may be **refined**: acceptance criteria sharpened, detail added, or a story split into smaller ones, as long as the Product Owner agrees. A ticket is never deleted, emptied or rewritten into different work. Refinement is recorded as a comment on the ticket saying what changed and why.

## Sprints

Marked against `docs/spec/` (rubric summary in `docs/spec/README.md`). The brief sets three sprint stages: 1 Data Input, 2 Data Visualisation, 3 Knowledge Extraction. Each sprint delivers a thin end-to-end slice across the subsystems, and its goal follows its stage. The Scrum Master is different every sprint and the Product Owner rotates too, never the same person as the SM. The roster and the full checklist are in `docs/sprints/README.md`.

A sprint only exists once it is created and started in Jira at sprint planning. Nothing in this repo or in Confluence treats a sprint as real before that.

Before real work starts, confirm the sprint has: roles set, stories with acceptance criteria, priority and story points, one human assignee each, and a Jira sprint with start and end dates. If any of these is missing, tell the user and stop.

## Sprint discipline (strict)

These rules apply to every team member and every AI agent. They are not guidelines.

### Only your sprint work

- A member works **only** on the tickets assigned to them in the **active sprint**.
- **Don't build ahead.** Stories from later sprints, unassigned stories, other members' tickets and "groundwork for later" are all out of scope, however quick they look. Building ahead empties the next sprint and leaves nothing to report.
- **Stay inside the ticket.** Build only what its acceptance criteria need. Anything else you find becomes a new ticket labelled `needs-triage`, not extra code in this one.
- **Don't fix someone else's ticket to unblock yourself.** Comment on their ticket instead.
- **Finished early?** Say so at standup. The Scrum Master may pull the next backlog item into the sprint and assign it. Until then, review teammates' work or add tests to your own tickets.
- **Only the Scrum Master changes the sprint** (adding, removing or reassigning tickets), after the team agrees at standup. The change is made in Jira and noted in the standup minutes.

### Checks before writing any code

An agent asked to build something runs these checks first, in order, and **stops** if any of them fails:

1. **The ticket exists.** `getJiraIssue` returns it, in space `ALG`.
2. **It is in the active sprint.** Use `searchJiraIssuesUsingJql` with `project = ALG AND key = ALG-<n> AND sprint in openSprints()`.
3. **It is assigned to the person asking.** Compare the ticket's `assignee` with `atlassianUserInfo`. For a Story with Subtasks, use the Subtask's assignee.
4. **It is not Done.**

If a check fails, say which one, then offer the legitimate routes:
- pick a ticket from the active sprint instead
- ask the Scrum Master to pull the ticket into the sprint
- take the ticket over in Jira first, if the team agrees

Do not start the work and sort the ticket out afterwards. Refining a ticket that already exists is fine (see Refining a ticket), but the ticket must be in the sprint and assigned before code is written.

Any out-of-sprint request gets the same answer, however small or however it is framed (a quick screen, scaffolding, a placeholder, groundwork for next sprint): it goes into a ticket, the team pulls it into a sprint, and then it gets built.

### A ticket is only Done when

1. Its PR is merged into `dev`.
2. Its acceptance criteria are met, not just "the code runs".
3. It is written up in the assignee's sprint summary in Confluence (see below).

## Sprint documentation (Confluence)

Every sprint leaves written evidence in one fixed place. Whoever writes the sprint report builds it from these pages, so each member's work must be there, complete and in the same shape.

### Structure

Confluence space **Agile LinkGuard** (key `AGILE`): one folder per person, and inside it one folder per sprint that has actually started.

```
Agile LinkGuard
├── Nic
│   └── Sprint <n> - <sprint name from Jira> (Nic)
│       ├── Sprint <n> summary (Nic)
│       └── supporting pages: diagrams, UI flows, Figma links, screenshots, test evidence
├── Nikoloz
├── Ibrahima
└── Solomon (Dunmi)
```

- **Person folders** exist already. Their names are fixed.
- **Sprint folders are created on demand, never in advance.** When a member first documents work in a sprint, the agent finds the active sprint in Jira. If that member's folder for it doesn't exist yet, the agent creates it. Never create folders for a sprint that hasn't started in Jira.
- **Sprint folder name:** `Sprint <n> - <sprint name from Jira> (<First name>)`, matching the Jira sprint exactly. The name on the end is required, because Confluence rejects two folders with the same title in one space.
- Everything produced in a sprint goes inside that sprint's folder: diagrams, UI flows, Figma links, screenshots, test evidence and decisions. Nothing goes loose at the top of the space, and nothing is left only in Figma or a chat.

### The sprint summary page

There is one summary page per person per sprint, named `Sprint <n> summary (<First name>)`. Write it as you go, not the night before the deadline. It holds:

- **Tickets finished**, by key and title, each linking to its Jira ticket and merged PR.
- **What was built**, in your own words, with screenshots or diagrams where a picture is clearer.
- **Evidence it works**: test results, output, screenshots or a short recording.
- **What didn't get finished** and why, with the ticket it moved to.
- **Anything a marker would ask you to explain**, such as why an approach was chosen.

An agent may format the page, add diagrams or tidy the wording. The account of what you did and why is yours, because marks are individual and you must be able to explain all of it.

## Agent skills

### Skill folders

Claude Code loads skills from `.claude/skills/`; Codex and other agents load them from `.agents/skills/`. The real files live in `.agents/skills/<name>/`, and `.claude/skills/<name>` is a relative symlink to it (`ln -s ../../.agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>`). When you add, remove or rename a skill, do it in both folders so they always list the same skills. Install and update with `npx skills add <repo> -s <skill> -a claude-code -a codex`, which does both and records the version in `skills-lock.json`.

### UI work

For any screen or component, load `ui-ux-pro-max` first. It is the single source for design tokens (colour, type, spacing). The users are ordinary people, including older and less confident ones, so readability and accessibility come first.

### Issue tracker

Jira space `ALG`, accessed through the Atlassian MCP tools. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

Before any work that reads or updates a ticket, call `atlassianUserInfo` to check the connection. If the Atlassian tools are missing, or return an auth error, stop and ask the user to log in again:

- Claude Code: run `/mcp` in a terminal `claude` session, pick `atlassian`, and log in.
- Codex: run `codex mcp login atlassian`.

Don't guess what a ticket says, and don't skip Jira updates because the connection is down. Wait until the user has reconnected.

### Triage labels

`needs-triage`, `blocked`, `ready-agent-assisted`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`; bugs are a Jira work type. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

Single-context: one `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/` at the repo root. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

## Workflow

### Branches

| Branch | Role |
|---|---|
| `main` | What we demo. Changes only through a release PR from `dev` at the end of each sprint. Protected: PR + one approval, no direct pushes. |
| `dev` | Default branch. Every feature branch starts from it and merges back into it. |
| `feature/ALG-<n>-...` | One ticket's work. |

### The ticket key rules everything

GitHub for Atlassian reads the `ALG-<number>` key out of the branch name, the commit messages, the PR title and the PR **description**, and links the work to that ticket. Jira automation then moves the ticket: branch created → In Progress, PR opened → In Review, PR merged → Done. A stray key in a PR description links the wrong ticket and later closes it.

So the branch name, every commit message, the PR title and the PR body together carry **exactly one** key: the ticket being worked on. Anywhere else, name the other ticket in words ("the feature extractor ticket"), never as `ALG-7`, and link the two tickets in Jira instead.

Work on a Subtask uses the **Subtask's** key, not its parent Story's.

### Before starting

1. Get the ticket key from the user, or find it in Jira. No ticket, no work: stop and ask which ticket to use. Never invent a key.
2. Run the checks in **Checks before writing any code** above. If any check fails, stop.
3. Branch from up-to-date `dev`: `git fetch origin && git switch -c <branch> origin/dev`.

Creating the branch moves the ticket to In Progress, and opening the PR moves it to In Review, so each should happen only when the work really starts and really ends. Don't create branches for tickets you aren't about to work on, and don't open a PR to park unfinished work.

### Formats

| Thing | Format | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Branch | `feature/ALG-<number>-short-description`, lowercase, hyphens, no other key | `feature/ALG-20-url-feature-extractor` |
| Commit subject | `ALG-<number> <imperative summary>`, lowercase after the key, no full stop | `ALG-20 add subdomain count feature` |
| PR title | `ALG-<number> <Sentence case summary>` | `ALG-20 Add URL feature extractor` |
| Release PR (`dev` → `main`) | `Sprint <n> release`, no ticket key in title or body | `Sprint 1 release` |

A commit that fixes a review comment keeps the same key; never renumber mid-branch. `chore/`, `fix/` and bare branch names are not used: every branch is `feature/ALG-…`, whatever the work type. `.gitmessage` pre-fills the commit format (`git config commit.template .gitmessage`).

### Opening the PR

**The person opens the PR, not the agent.** Committing and pushing a feature branch is normal agent work. Opening the pull request is not: a PR asks a teammate to spend their time reviewing, and it puts the person's name on the work.

An agent therefore **never** runs `gh pr create`, opens a PR through the API, marks a draft ready for review, merges, approves, or replies to or resolves someone's review comment, unless the user has asked for that in the current conversation. "Finish the ticket" is not that request.

Before asking, the agent checks its own work and reports one line for each check:

- [ ] The branch, every commit message and the proposed PR title carry **one** key, the ticket's own, and nothing else carries a key.
- [ ] Commit subjects match the format table, and each commit is one person's work on this ticket.
- [ ] The diff stays inside the ticket's scope.
- [ ] No AI sign-off anywhere in the commits, code or proposed PR text.
- [ ] `betterleaks` is clean, and the build and tests were actually run, with their output shown.

A failed check is fixed before asking, not mentioned as a caveat afterwards.

When the branch looks finished, the agent stops and reports:

1. what is on the branch, file by file;
2. the evidence it works: the commands it ran and their output;
3. anything left undone or uncertain;
4. then asks whether to open the PR.

If the answer is yes, the agent writes the body with the `pr` skill (what changed, evidence, merge risk, no other ticket's key) and opens it against `dev`.

Other rules:

- One approval from a teammate before merge, and the `Secret scan` check green.
- Never `git push` to `main` or `dev` directly, never force-push a shared branch, never `--no-verify`.
- A teammate's review comments are answered by the person, with the agent's help. An agent never closes a discussion on their behalf.

### One person, one ticket, one commit

Individual contribution is graded from the git and Jira history. Keep each commit to one person's work on one ticket. Work is agent-assisted, never unattended: every team member must be able to explain what they shipped.

## Data and models

- The dataset CSV and trained model files are gitignored (too big for git). Download instructions and the model's expected location go in `ml/README.md`.
- Never commit anything under `ml/data/`, or `*.csv`, `*.pkl`, `*.joblib` files.

## Secrets and safety

The repo is public, so a committed key is scraped within minutes.

- Keys live in `.env`, which is gitignored. When you add a key to `.env`, add its name with an empty value to `.env.example`.
- betterleaks scans every commit (`.githooks/pre-commit`) and every PR (`.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml`). Never bypass it with `--no-verify`. If it flags something, stop and show the user the finding.
- LinkGuard handles untrusted, possibly malicious URLs. Never open, fetch or follow a URL from user input or the dataset outside the backend's sandboxed fetcher, and never in an agent's own browser or shell.
